photo_alt: A Beneteau Oceanis 34.1 sailing on blue water
description: A small, light boat that answers every touch of the helm. Three cabins and one head suit a beginner crew of four with an instructor, and every sail control is easy to see and reach.

photo_alt: A Beneteau Oceanis 38.1 under sail off the coast
description: Easy to handle with a small crew, with twin wheels and a clear deck. Our usual boat for first skippers on the Flotilla course.

photo_alt: A Bavaria C38 sailing in a green bay
description: A newer Bavaria with a wide stern and a big cockpit table. Handy for mooring practice in Fethiye bay and for a family charter afterwards.

photo_alt: A Dufour 390 at anchor off a marina
description: Quick and well balanced, with the mainsheet led to the helm. A good boat for learning sail trim.

photo_alt: The cockpit and twin wheels of a Hanse 410
description: A self-tacking jib and every line led to the helm, so two people can sail her. Based in Göcek for charter between our courses.

photo_alt: A Jeanneau Sun Odyssey 410 under sail at sunset
description: Walk-around side decks make it safe to move forward on a heeling boat, which is why we like her for passages and night watches.

photo_alt: The cockpit of a Hanse 460 moored in a marina
description: A big, stiff boat for open-sea legs and Yachtmaster weeks, with room for a crew of eight on long passages.

photo_alt: A Jeanneau Sun Odyssey 490 at anchor in a bay
description: Our largest monohull. Stable and comfortable on long legs, with five cabins for bigger crews and charter groups.

photo_alt: A Lagoon 40 catamaran moored in a marina
description: A catamaran for families and groups: level decks, a big saloon and twin engines that make harbour manoeuvres easy. We use it for charter and for catamaran handling practice.
Spacious and stable, with a flybridge helm and a big cockpit. For charter groups who want comfort as well as good sailing.
